methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI bills faced a logjam in the General Assembly due to a Trump executive order, but Congress is working to fill the gap
signals.signal_reading: Federal policy threats blocking state AI regulation while also endangering broadband funding creates a dual barrier for rural Virginia—neither the infrastructure foundation nor the policy framework for distributed AI capability can develop, reinforcing concentration in already-connected metros.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA represents institutional commitment to community-scale AI education beyond elite tech workers, signaling potential for peer-driven learning networks that could distribute capability through Richmond's diverse workforce sectors.

signals.title: RC-RV partners with ed2go to launch innovative, on-demand workforce training programs - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Platform-delivered workforce training via ed2go offers shallow, on-demand skill acquisition rather than deep capability building—accessible distribution without the peer networks or institutional depth needed to create lasting regional AI fluency in traditionally underserved Southwest Virginia.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Competitive pressure on Richmond's young workforce to adopt AI reveals metro-concentrated anxiety and adaptation cycles that don't yet extend to rural regions, indicating capability development clustering where labor markets already demand it.

signals.title: Virginia’s AI Data Center Gravy Train Shows Signs of Slowing - Bloomberg Law News
signals.signal_reading: NoVA's data center slowdown doesn't redistribute AI infrastructure—it consolidates what exists while halting expansion, freezing the current concentrated geography of computational power and the technical expertise required to operate it.
